target_customer: Solar asset managers and their security monitoring providers
problem: Solar sites suffer theft and intrusions, and security cameras generate false alarms and silent failures; managers want detection without replacing hardware.
product_category: Computer vision intrusion detection for remote outdoor sites

founders.name: F-G Fernandez
previous_startups: Quack AI (developer onboarding companion, per a YC launch post, identity inferred from same user ID)
founders.background_notes: YC page says he is a former top PyTorch contributor and published papers without a PhD.

technical_complexity.rationale: Running low-false-alarm intrusion detection across heterogeneous existing cameras and detecting camera failures needs solid vision work, and the founder has field vision deployment experience.

defensibility.rationale: Camera-agnostic software is replicable by video analytics vendors; a per-site relationship with asset managers adds modest switching cost.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Solar video analytics vendors existed, but no evidence was found of them copying or acquiring Rimward.

market_need_then: Solar farms attract theft per industry articles, but undated; no dated 2023 evidence of spend was found.

branding.domain_note: Uses rimward.ai; domain history not found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Direct: security software for solar portfolios using the cameras you already have

brand_strength.rationale: No press on the brand; only a Station F startup list mention was seen as a headline.

outcome_analysis: Rimward is a one-person Paris startup selling camera-agnostic intrusion detection to solar operators, led by a computer vision researcher with field wildfire detection experience. No shutdown, acquisition or verified funding was found. Traction is unknown, so outcome is unresolved.
notes: Funding unverified: vcbacked lists $900K pre-seed in September 2023 with Y Combinator, Sequoia Capital, Entrepreneurs First, Unpopular Ventures and AGORANOV; a single aggregator, so not recorded as a round. Competitor names (Irisity, DAVANTIS, Hikvision) come from undated pages, so the dated list is empty; DAVANTIS has a March 2022 case study but not as of founding evidence of traction. Education not found. Completeness pass: the 900K pre-seed rests on a single database (VCBacked); a cross-check search found no second source.
